summary: Owned units s0222–s0243 state no birth, age, or Chinese calendar year. They do record Huizhi's undated bamboo and Shan-yin anecdotes, Dai Kui then in Shan, a night reading of 高士傳贊 that names 井丹 and 長卿, Huizhi as 黃門侍郎 who 棄官東歸, joint critical illness, 獻之卒, and Huizhi's 月餘亦卒 from a burst back abscess. Every supplied Western interval is invented: AD 270–300, 58–88, and BC 179–117 date later quotations of Zuo Si, Jing Dan, and Sima Xiangru as if they were those men's lives; AD 360–395 and 370–386 close undated Dai Kui and reading scenes; AD 376–396 copies the 太元 reign of Emperor Xiaowu onto offices, illness, deaths, attestations, and hints. The relative death sequence is the only supported chronology and must be kept. No owned check is approved.
